newsitem.title: INDIA: Cotton-Indian supply seen comfortable, prices easy.
newsitem.headline: Cotton-Indian supply seen comfortable, prices easy.

text.p: Supplies of Indian cotton upto next October, when the new crop arrives in the market, is comfortable enough to keep prices under pressure, traders said on Thursday.
They said state procurement agencies held enough stocks with them as carryover for the 1997/98 (October-September) season.
Traders said some cotton crop sown early in the southern state of Karnataka and the western state of Gujarat was expected to arrive by the end of this month.
"But the quantity will be very small," said a trader.

Traders said they expected prices to remain easy despite the fag end of the 1996/97 season. The bulk of the current season's crop, estimated at 16.78 bales (one bale is 170 kg) had already been marketed.
In the week to Thursday, cotton prices fell on the local market as the satisfactory progress of monsoon rains in cotton-producing states prompted selling by traders.
"The progress of monsoon rains has been satisfactory and brightened the prospects for the 1997/98 (October/September) crop," one trader said.
"But it's too early to predict the size of the new crop at this juncture," he said.
In spot, Bengal-deshi slid 5.0 rupees to 1,025/1,050 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), while Punjab saw-ginned lost 20 rupees to 1,825/1,860 rupees per maund.
Punjab F-414 fell 15/20 rupees to 2,050/2,075 rupees per maund. Among Gujarat varieties Kalyan cotton fell 100 rupees to 13,800/14,200 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
The superior variety of long-staple Gujarat Sankar-4 lost 500 rupees to 19,000/20,000 rupees per candy. ($=35.79 rupees)
